mainTopic: Women and the marriage bans of כהונה, and the money rights (כתובה, מזונות) of women in forbidden marriages.
overview: The גמרא tries to prove from טומאת כהנים that רב יהודה's rule makes women liable even for a לאו שאין שוה בכל. The proof is rejected in two versions. Each version ties the verse "בני אהרן" to the words "לא יקחו" in a different way. Next, a story asks whether women who are כשרות are warned against marrying פסולין. רב פפא tries to prove it from the משנה of the ten lineages, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects that proof. Then רב אידי בר אבין rules in the name of רב that they are not warned. רב ששת then teaches from a ברייתא that a woman who was a שניה to her first husband gets no כתובה, not even from the יבם. After that, רבי יוחנן rules that a woman in a marriage forbidden to a כהן gets no מזונות while her husband is alive. The ברייתא that gives her מזונות is about after his death. Finally, a ברייתא contrasts Torah-level forbidden marriages, where she keeps her money rights but becomes פסולה, with שניות, where she loses them but stays כשרה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר begins explaining why, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A proof from the impurity of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings טומאה as evidence that רב יהודה's rule includes women even in a לאו שאין שוה בכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the ban on becoming impure. It does not apply to everyone, since only כהנים have it. The Torah had to write "sons of Aaron" to show that daughters are not included. So without that verse, we would have said women are also obligated. Why would we have said that? Isn't it because of רב יהודה's rule in the name of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a proof. Even for a ban that only applies to some people (כהנים), we would have included women if the Torah had not excluded them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah went out of its way to write "בני אהרן" and not daughters. That implies a default where women would have been obligated. The גמרא suggests this default comes from רב יהודה's rule, which would show that the rule covers even a לאו שאין שוה בכל.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity; here, the ban on כהנים becoming impure from a dead body
A prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
I would have thought (an early assumption)

phrases.english: But there is impurity,
phrases.notes: He means the ban on כהנים becoming impure from a dead body (ויקרא 21:1).

phrases.english: which is a prohibition that is not equal for all,
and the reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"sons of Aaron", and not daughters of Aaron;
but if not for this,
I would have said women are obligated.
What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב?
phrases.english: Is it not because of what רב יהודה said in the name of רב?
phrases.notes: This is his rule that the Torah made women equal to men for all punishments.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי טוּמְאָה, דְּלָאו שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether רב יהודה's rule covers a לאו שאין שוה בכל.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יהודה's rule makes women liable even in a לאו שאין שוה בכל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse "בני אהרן" was needed to exclude daughters from the ban on טומאה, which implies they would otherwise have been included.

steps.title: The early assumption came from "they may not take"
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. We would have included women in טומאה because of the words "לא יקחו", not because of רב יהודה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. That assumption comes from what we learn from "they may not take".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a different source for the idea that women might have been included in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא יקחו" teaches that women are part of the marriage bans of כהונה. From that, one might have thought they are part of all the laws of כהנים, including טומאה. So the verse "בני אהרן" was needed for that reason, and the proof for רב יהודה's rule falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn (from a verse or source)
"They may not take", the verse about whom כהנים may not marry

phrases.english: No, it is because we learn from "they may not take."
phrases.notes: This is the verse about the women כהנים may not marry (ויקרא 21:7).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 1 by giving another source for the assumption.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not reject רב יהודה's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that women would be included in טומאה can be explained by "לא יקחו" instead of by רב יהודה's rule.

steps.title: Another version: the verse about taking was needed
steps.stepSummary: A second version flips the comparison. The verse about taking was needed so that we would not learn the marriage bans from טומאה and leave women out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: the verse about taking was needed. You might have thought we should learn from impurity, so the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the answer. Here, the verse about marriage is the one that needed to be written, because otherwise we would have copied the rule of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, טומאה applies only to males. Without a special teaching, we would have said the marriage bans also apply only to males. The verse about taking tells us that this is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking, meaning marriage
You might have thought
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: In step 2, women's inclusion in the marriage bans might have spread to טומאה. In this version it is the reverse: the rule of טומאה might have spread to the marriage bans.

phrases.english: There are those who say: the verse about taking was needed,
since it would have entered your mind to say:
let us learn from impurity,
phrases.notes: So the marriage bans would apply only to men, just like טומאה.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the rejection in step 2, with the direction of learning reversed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Explains the need for the verse in a way that does not depend on רב יהודה's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse about taking was written so that we would not learn from טומאה. So no proof can be drawn for רב יהודה's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from טומאה does not stand in either version. Its need for a special verse can be explained through "לא יקחו" and not through רב יהודה's rule.

steps.title: The people of הינצבו ask about כשרות marrying פסולין
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע come to the town of רב אידי בר אבין. They are asked whether women who are כשרות are warned against marrying men who are פסולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא son of רב יהושע arrived at הינצבו, the place of רב אידי בר אבין. They were asked: are women who are fit (כשרות) warned against marrying men who are disqualified (פסולין), or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story that opens a new question. It sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have discussed bans on a כהן marrying certain women. Now the question goes the other way: is a כשרה woman herself warned against marrying a פסול? The answer will come in the following lines.

keyTerms.meaning: They happened to arrive
Were they warned (given a prohibition)
Women who are fit to marry a כהן
Men who are disqualified from כהונה

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
arrived at Hintzevu,
to the place of Rav Idi bar Avin.
They asked them:
Were fit women warned against marrying disqualified men,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינַּיְיהוּ: הוּזְהֲרוּ כְּשֵׁרוֹת לְהִנָּשֵׂא לִפְסוּלִין, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic through a story, after the discussion of טומאה ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman fit for כהונה is herself warned against marrying a man who is פסול.

steps.title: רב פפא brings a proof from the list of ten lineages
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes the משנה of the ten lineages that came up from בבל. It lists which groups may marry each other and never says a כהנת may marry a חלל. He takes this as proof that she is forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: You learned this in a משנה. Ten family types went up from בבל: כהנים, לוים, ישראלים, חללים, גרים, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקי, and אסופי. כהנים, לוים and ישראלים may marry each other. לוים, ישראלים, חללים, גרים and freed slaves may marry each other. גרים, freed slaves, ממזרים, נתינים, שתוקי and אסופי may marry each other. But the משנה does not teach that a כהנת may marry a חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 4 with a proof from a משנה. That משנה never allows a כהנת to marry a חלל, so he concludes that she is warned against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists groups that may marry each other. A חלל appears in the middle group with ישראלים, but not in the first group with כהנים. רב פפא reads that silence as meaning a כהנת may not marry a חלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Family lineages, the status groups of the Jewish people
Son of a כהן from a forbidden marriage. He loses כהונה status.
A child who knows his mother but not his father
A foundling, a child found abandoned whose parents are unknown
Gibeonites, a group barred from marrying into the Jewish people
"It does not teach". The proof is built on what the משנה leaves out.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them: You learned it in a Mishnah:
Ten lineages went up from Babylonia:
Kohanim, Levites, and Israelites,
chalalim, converts, and freed slaves,
and mamzerim, Gibeonites, children of unknown fathers, and foundlings.
Kohanim, Levites, Israelites:
are permitted to marry one another.
Levites, Israelites, chalalim, converts, freed slaves:
are permitted to marry one another.
Converts, freed slaves, and mamzerim,
Gibeonites, children of unknown fathers, and foundlings:
are permitted to marry one another.
But a kohenes marrying a chalal is not taught.
phrases.notes: רב פפא means that since the משנה never allows it, it must be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4 by bringing a משנה as evidence.
steps.raayaObject: That women who are כשרות (a כהנת) are warned against marrying men who are פסולין (a חלל)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the ten lineages (קידושין 69a). It does not list a כהנת as permitted to a חלל.

steps.title: The list only names groups that can marry each other both ways
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects the proof. The משנה only lists groups where the men of each group may marry the women of the other group and the reverse. A כהן may not marry a חללה, so the pair כהנים and חללים could not appear together anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said to him: The משנה only teaches cases where these men may marry those women and those men may marry these women. A כהן is forbidden to marry a חללה if he wants to, so the משנה does not list them together.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע shows that the silence in the משנה proves nothing about a כהנת. The groups were left apart for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only puts two groups together when marriage works in both directions. A כהן marrying a חללה is clearly forbidden, so כהנים and חללים could never share a group. That is true even if a כהנת were allowed to marry a חלל, so the משנה proves nothing. The next step settles the question.

keyTerms.meaning: They marry (literally: they take)
A female חלל, forbidden to a כהן
It is forbidden to him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said to him:
Anywhere that these marry from those
and those marry from these, it teaches.
phrases.notes: He means marriage must work both ways: men of group A with women of group B, and men of B with women of A.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן, כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ בָּעֵי לְמִינְסַב חֲלָלָה
phrases.english: A kohen, since if he wanted to marry a chalalah,
she is forbidden to him, it does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּהָנֵי נָסְבִי מֵהָנֵי וְהָנֵי נָסְבִי מֵהָנֵי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's proof from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The ruling itself is left undecided.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה only groups lineages that can marry in both directions. Leaving out כהנים and חללים is explained by the man's ban on a חללה, not by any ban on a כהנת.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין settles it: women who are fit are not warned
steps.stepSummary: The two רבנן bring the question to רב אידי בר אבין. He quotes רב יהודה in the name of רב: women who are כשרות are not warned against marrying men who are פסולין. So a כהנת may marry a חלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רב אידי בר אבין. He said to them: Children, this is what רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Women who are fit were not warned against marrying men who are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from step 4 gets its final answer. רב quoted by רב יהודה rules that the prohibition is not on the women, so a כהנת may marry a חלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on marrying a פסול falls on the כהן, not on the woman. So the woman who is כשרה has no warning against marrying a man who is פסול. This also shows that רב פפא's reading of the משנה was wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Children, youngsters. A friendly way an older teacher speaks to younger scholars.
They were not warned. There is no prohibition placed on them.
Women who are fit, like a כהנת of proper lineage
Men who are disqualified from כהונה, like a חלל

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רב: a כהנת may marry a חלל. The marriage bans of כהונה are on the man, not on the woman who is כשרה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב פפא's proof. רב פפא wanted to show she IS warned, but the final answer is that she is NOT warned.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין.
phrases.english: They came before Rav Idi bar Avin.
He said to them: Children,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: this is what Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Fit women were not warned against marrying disqualified men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 5 was rejected in step 6, the question is settled by a tradition from רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Women who are כשרות are not warned against marrying men who are פסולין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהנת may marry a חלל. The prohibition belongs to the כהן alone.

steps.title: Does a woman forbidden only to her husband get a marriage contract from the יבם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about שניות מדברי סופרים. The people of בירי ask רב ששת about a woman who was a שניה to her husband but is not a שניה to the יבם. Does she collect a כתובה from the יבם?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Secondary relatives forbidden by rabbinic law, and so on. The people of בירי asked רב ששת: If a woman is a secondary relative of the husband but not of the יבם, does she get a כתובה from the יבם or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. The גמרא quotes the משנה about rabbinically forbidden relatives, and the people of בירי ask a new question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her first marriage was forbidden by the רבנן, so she gets no כתובה from her husband. Now she falls to a יבם who is allowed to her. The question is whether her new, permitted marriage gives her a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary forbidden relatives, forbidden by the רבנן rather than by the Torah
By rabbinic law (literally: from the words of the scribes)
The brother of a man who died without children, who may marry the widow
The marriage contract payment a wife receives
They asked him

phrases.english: Secondary relatives by rabbinic law, etc.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ בְּנֵי בֵירֵי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: The people of Biri asked of Rav Sheshet:
A secondary relative to the husband but not a secondary relative to the yavam,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה מִיָּבָם אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: does she have a marriage contract from the yavam or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ בְּנֵי בֵירֵי מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of כשרות and פסולין and returns to a new line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a woman who was a שניה only to her husband collects a כתובה from the יבם, who is permitted to her.

steps.title: The two sides of the marriage-contract question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the question is hard. Maybe she gets nothing, because the כתובה in יבום comes from the first husband's property, and she had no כתובה from him. Or maybe she gets one, because the רבנן made the יבם pay whenever the first husband's property cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Master said that her marriage contract is paid from the first husband's property, maybe she has none. Or perhaps, since the Rabbis arranged that if she has nothing from the first husband she collects from the second, she does have one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two possible ways to view her case. It does not answer yet. This sets up the reply that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: her כתובה in יבום is really the first husband's, and he owed her none, so she gets nothing. Side two: when the first husband's property gives her nothing, the רבנן made the second husband (the יבם) pay. Maybe that covers her case too, since she gets nothing from the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of her first husband
The רבנן made an enactment (a תקנה)
Or perhaps, which opens the second side of a question

phrases.english: Since the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתוּבָּתָהּ עַל נִכְסֵי בַּעְלָהּ הָרִאשׁוֹן — לֵית לַהּ,
phrases.english: her marriage contract is from the property of her first husband, she does not have one.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ לֵית לַהּ מֵרִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since if she has none from the first,

phrases.aramaic: תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן מִשֵּׁנִי — אִית לַהּ?
phrases.english: the Rabbis enacted for her from the second, she does have one?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר מָר: כְּתוּבָּתָהּ עַל נִכְסֵי בַּעְלָהּ הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the יבם's כתובה only a stand-in for the first husband's, so she gets none? Or does the רבנן's enactment make the יבם pay whenever she gets nothing from the first husband?

steps.title: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells the people of בירי that a ברייתא already answers their question: a woman who was a שניה to her first husband gets no כתובה, not even from the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned this in a ברייתא. Her כתובה is paid from her first husband's property. And if she was a שניה to that husband, she gets nothing, not even from the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from Step 8 by quoting a ברייתא that settles it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כתובה normally comes from the first husband's property. If she was a שניה to the first husband, she gets nothing even from the יבם. So the second side of Step 9 is rejected: the רבנן did not make the יבם pay for a woman who had no כתובה from the first husband.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a ברייתא)
The property of her first husband
A relative forbidden only by the רבנן (a secondary forbidden relative)
The brother-in-law who marries his brother's widow

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it:
Her marriage contract is paid from the property of her first husband.
And if she was a secondary forbidden relative to the husband,
phrases.notes: "The husband" here means the first husband, the one who died.

phrases.english: she does not have one even from the yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Steps 8 and 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She gets no כתובה from the יבם, because she had none from her first husband.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא imply the יבם sometimes pays?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the word "even" in the ברייתא suggests that in some case the woman does collect from the יבם, but the ברייתא never mentioned such a case.
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, is there a case where she does get a כתובה from the יבם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא: "even from the יבם" sounds like the יבם normally pays, yet the ברייתא just said the כתובה comes from the first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first line puts the כתובה only on the first husband's property. Then "even from the יבם" implies there is a normal case where the יבם pays. The גמרא asks where that case is in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from the way it is said

phrases.english: By implication, there is a case
where she does have it from the yavam?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase "even from the יבם" in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "Even" implies a normal case where the יבם pays, but the ברייתא only spoke of the first husband's property.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing a line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא is missing words. When the first husband left no property, the רבנן made the יבם pay. But a שניה gets nothing even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing something, and this is what it means: Her כתובה is paid from her first husband's property. If there is nothing from the first husband, the רבנן arranged for her to be paid from the second (the יבם). But if she was a שניה to the first husband, she gets nothing, not even from the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adding a missing line to the ברייתא, which explains when the יבם pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added line says that if the first husband left no property, the יבם pays. Now "even from the יבם" makes sense: a שניה loses even this backup. It also confirms that the backup only helps a woman who had a valid כתובה from the first husband.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words, and we fill them in
And this is what it teaches
They (the רבנן) instituted

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the יבם's payment is a separate, new כתובה that any woman gets. It is only a backup for a כתובה she already had from the first husband. A שניה never had one, so there is nothing to back up.
steps.whatToRemember: A כתובה in יבום comes from the first husband's property. The יבם pays only as a backup, and a שניה to the first husband gets nothing at all.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
Her marriage contract is paid from the property of her first husband,
and if she has nothing from the first,
they instituted it for her from the second.
And if she was a secondary forbidden relative to the husband,
she does not have one even from the yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding missing words to the text (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to give no case where the יבם pays, so "even" made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא includes a case where the יבם pays (no property from the first husband), and a שניה loses even that.

steps.title: Do forbidden wives of a כהן get food support?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רבי יוחנן whether a woman in a marriage forbidden to a כהן gets מזונות from her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רבי יוחנן: A widow married to a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or חלוצה married to a regular כהן: do they get food support, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי אלעזר asks about food support (מזונות) for women in marriages forbidden to כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These marriages are forbidden to a כהן, but the woman still gets a כתובה. The question is whether her right to food support follows the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
The High Priest
A regular כהן
A widow released from יבום by חליצה
Food support a husband owes his wife

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rabbi Yochanan:
A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a chalutza married to a regular priest,
do they have food support
or do they not have food support?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: food support in forbidden marriages, after the discussion of כתובה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether women in marriages forbidden to a כהן get מזונות.

steps.title: If she lives with him, the answer is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the question is about. If she lives with him, he must divorce her right away, so of course she gets no food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say she is living with him, he is under orders to get up and divorce her. Would she get food support?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's question. In the simple case it seems too obvious to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the couple is together, the husband must divorce her immediately. Giving her food support would only keep the forbidden marriage going. So the question needs a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say
"Get up and divorce her": the husband must end the marriage right away

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that she is living with him,
he stands under the order "get up and divorce her,"
does she have food support?
phrases.notes: This is said with surprise. Of course she doesn't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what case רבי אלעזר's question in Step 13 could be about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי אלעזר's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she lives with him, he must divorce her right away, so food support is obviously not given and there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The case: he went overseas and she borrowed for food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question is about a husband who went overseas, while she borrowed money and spent it on food. Must he repay?
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed where he went overseas, and she borrowed money and ate. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a case where the question is real. It then sets up the two sides of the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the husband away, he cannot divorce her now, and the food is already eaten. The question is whether he must pay back her loan. This is no longer obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a different case)
Overseas; a faraway place
She borrowed and ate

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where he went overseas,
and she borrowed money and ate.
What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, שֶׁהָלַךְ הוּא לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question seemed to be about a couple living together, where the answer is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about a husband who is away, where she borrowed for food and wants him to repay.

steps.title: The two sides: food is part of the כתובה, or food delays the divorce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out why the question is hard. Food support may be a condition of the כתובה, so she gets it too. Or a כתובה is different because it helps her leave, while food support may make her stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is food support a condition of the כתובה, so since she has a כתובה she also has food support? Or maybe: the כתובה, which lets her take it and leave, she does get. But food support, which might make her stay with him, she does not get?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible ways to look at the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: food support is one of the conditions of the כתובה, so it follows the כתובה. Side two: the רבנן gave her a כתובה because it pushes her to take the money and leave the forbidden marriage. Food support does the opposite, because it lets her stay comfortably, so it may not be given.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition of the כתובה; obligations that come with it
Or perhaps
To take (the money) and leave
She will stay on with him

phrases.english: Is food support a condition of the marriage contract,

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאִית לַהּ כְּתוּבָה אִית לַהּ מְזוֹנֵי,
phrases.english: so since she has a marriage contract, she has food support,
or perhaps:
the marriage contract, which is for taking and leaving, she has,

phrases.aramaic: מְזוֹנֵי, דִּלְמָא תִּיעַכַּב גַּבֵּיהּ — לֵית לַהּ?
phrases.english: but food support, where she might stay with him, she does not have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question asked in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether food support follows the כתובה as one of its conditions, or is withheld because it would keep her in the forbidden marriage.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: she gets no food support
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that she does not get food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: She does not get it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers רבי אלעזר: the forbidden wife gets no food support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the second side of Step 16. She keeps her כתובה, which helps her leave, but gets no food support, which could make her stay. So even when the husband is overseas, he does not have to repay her food loan.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not have (the right)

steps.whatToRemember: A woman in a marriage forbidden to a כהן still gets a כתובה but not מזונות. The רבנן want her to leave the marriage, not stay in it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the כתובה and מזונות can be split. Each one is judged by whether it pushes her out of the forbidden marriage or keeps her in it.

phrases.english: He said to him: She does not have it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Steps 13 to 16, choosing the second side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She gets no מזונות, because food support might keep her in the forbidden marriage.

steps.title: A ברייתא says she does get food support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling using a ברייתא that says she does get מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: she does have food support!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from step 17 by quoting a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the woman in a forbidden marriage does not get מזונות. A ברייתא says she does. A ruling by an אמורא should not contradict a ברייתא, so the גמרא needs to explain the conflict.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה
She has (the right to food support)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: she has [food support]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that she gets no מזונות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא directly states she does get מזונות, so it contradicts רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא is talking about after his death
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא refers to food support after the husband dies, not during his lifetime.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא is talking about a different time: after the husband has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the husband is alive, the marriage is forbidden and he must divorce her, so she gets no מזונות. After he dies, the forbidden relationship has ended. Then her right to food support as a widow, a condition of the כתובה, can apply. So the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן do not really argue.

keyTerms.meaning: When that ברייתא was taught. This limits a ברייתא to a specific case.
After death (of the husband)

phrases.english: When that was taught — it was after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a different time (after the husband's death)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to give her food support while married to him, against רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא gives her food support only after he dies. During his life she gets none, as רבי יוחנן said.

steps.title: Second version: רבי יוחנן answers from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבי יוחנן answers רבי אלעזר by quoting a ברייתא that says she does get food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: He (רבי יוחנן) said to him, a ברייתא teaches that she has food support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second way the conversation went. Here רבי יוחנן answers the question the other way, relying on a ברייתא that says she does get food support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי יוחנן ruled she gets nothing, and the גמרא raised the ברייתא against him. In this version רבי יוחנן himself relies on the ברייתא. This sets up רבי אלעזר's objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say. This introduces a second version of a discussion.

phrases.english: Some say:
He said to him: It is taught: she has [food support].
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, answering רבי אלעזר's question, just like in the first version.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִית דְּאָמַר: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, תַּנְיָא: יֵשׁ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the exchange of steps 17-19 in a different version
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that she gets no מזונות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says she has מזונות.

steps.title: He must divorce her, so no food support
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר objects that the husband stands under an order to get up and divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is standing under the order 'get up and divorce her'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר pushes back. A husband who is required to divorce her right away should not have to feed her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the law requires the husband to end the marriage, making him pay for her food would treat the forbidden marriage as normal. So רבי אלעזר argues that she should get no מזונות, despite the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Get up and divorce (her). This is the order to end a forbidden marriage immediately.
He stands (in that situation)

phrases.english: But he stands in [the status of] 'get up and divorce'?
phrases.notes: Literally 'get up and send out': the court tells him he must divorce her right away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's citation in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical pushback based on the duty to divorce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא would require him to feed her during the marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man who must divorce her immediately should not owe her food support.

steps.title: But the ברייתא still says she gets it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן presses back: the ברייתא still clearly says she has food support.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, a ברייתא teaches that she has food support!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is not moved. A logical argument does not cancel an explicit ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר gave a reason why she should get nothing. But the ברייתא's words still say she does. So the contradiction has to be solved by explaining the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But then (how do you explain...). This presses a challenge again.

phrases.english: But then, isn't it taught: she has [food support]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge after the reply of step 21
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's explicit words still contradict him, no matter how good his logic is.

steps.title: Again: the ברייתא means after his death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the ברייתא refers to the time after the husband's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: Just like in the first version, the answer is that the ברייתא means after the husband dies. Both versions end in the same place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions reach the same ruling. During the husband's life she gets no מזונות. After his death she can collect support. The only difference is who argued which side and how the conversation went.

keyTerms.meaning: Death

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the ruling is the same. A woman in a forbidden marriage gets no food support while her husband is alive. The ברייתא that gives her support is about after his death.

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed challenge of step 22, matching step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to after the husband's death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא gives her food support during the marriage.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers only to after his death.

steps.title: Torah-level forbidden marriages: she keeps her money rights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that women in marriages forbidden by the Torah to a כהן get a כתובה and its benefits. She and her child become disqualified, and he is forced to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A widow married to a כהן גדול, or a divorcee or חלוצה married to a regular כהן, gets her כתובה, produce, food support and worn clothing. She is disqualified, her child is disqualified, and the court forces him to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists the rights and status of a woman in a marriage that the Torah forbids to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the marriage is forbidden by the Torah, she does not lose her money rights: כתובה, payment for produce, מזונות and בלאות. Her status is damaged, though. She becomes a חללה and her child is a חלל. The court also forces the husband to end the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow married to a כהן גדול, forbidden by the Torah
A divorcee and a woman released by חליצה, both forbidden to any כהן
A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
Worn-out items she brought into the marriage, which she gets back
The court forces him to divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא lists מזונות among her rights. Do not read this as arguing with רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא lists what she has a claim to, and the גמרא just explained that the food support applies after his death.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A widow [married] to a High Priest,
a divorcee or a חלוצה to a common priest —
she has a marriage contract, produce,
phrases.notes: 'Produce' means payment for the produce of her property that her husband used.

phrases.english: food support, worn clothing,
and she is disqualified, and her child is disqualified,
phrases.notes: She can no longer marry a כהן, and her son cannot serve as a כהן.

phrases.english: and they force him to divorce [her].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the rights of women in forbidden marriages
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In Torah-level forbidden marriages to a כהן, she keeps כתובה, produce, מזונות and בלאות. She and her child become disqualified, and he is forced to divorce her.

steps.title: Rabbinic-level forbidden relatives: no money rights, but no disqualification
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא rules that women forbidden only by rabbinic law (שניות) get none of the money rights, but she and her child remain fit. He is still forced to divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Secondary relatives forbidden by rabbinic law: she has no כתובה, no produce, no food support and no worn clothing. She is fit, her child is fit, and the court forces him to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and compares the Torah-level case with the case of relatives that the Rabbis forbade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases come out opposite. In the Torah case she keeps her money but loses her status. In the rabbinic case she loses her money rights but keeps her status, and so does her child. In both cases he must divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary relatives, marriages forbidden only by the Rabbis
By rabbinic law
Fit (she may still marry a כהן)
Her child is fit (for כהונה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This surprising flip, where the lighter prohibition loses the money and the stricter one keeps it, is what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר starts to explain in the next step.

phrases.english: Secondary relatives by rabbinic law —
she has no marriage contract, nor produce,
nor food support, nor worn clothing,
and she is fit, and her child is fit,
and they force him to divorce [her].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא, contrasting with step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For rabbinic-level forbidden relatives, she gets no כתובה, produce, מזונות or בלאות. She and her child stay fit, and he is forced to divorce her.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר begins explaining the reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר starts to explain why a widow married to a כהן גדול gets a כתובה: both he and she become disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: Why did they say a widow married to a כהן גדול has a כתובה? Because he is disqualified and she is disqualified. And any place where he is disqualified and she is disqualified...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר begins to give the reason behind the ברייתא's ruling. His sentence is not finished yet, so this step is setting up the rule that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He points out that in the Torah-level case, both sides suffer: the husband becomes disqualified, and the wife becomes a חללה. He starts to turn this into a general rule ('any place where...'). The ending of that rule comes after this section.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason
Disqualified
Any place, in every case. This introduces a general rule.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
For what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל יֵשׁ לָהּ כְּתוּבָּה —
phrases.english: a widow [married] to a High Priest has a marriage contract —
because he is disqualified and she is disqualified.
phrases.notes: He is barred from serving in the בית המקדש because of this marriage, and she becomes a חללה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא פָּסוּל וְהִיא פְּסוּלָה —
phrases.english: And any place where he is disqualified and she is disqualified —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling in step 24
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the Torah-level case both he and she are disqualified. This is the basis for her getting a כתובה, and the full rule continues after this section.
